status: weak-field gravitomagnetic admission test with Earth-orbit witness; no unique Spin(2,3) prediction

physicsSplit.massMultipoles: the scalar geopotential and its C_lm/S_lm coefficients generate gravitoelectric orbital perturbations such as J2 nodal precession
physicsSplit.currentDipole: the source angular momentum J generates the off-diagonal metric/spin-connection sector and Lense-Thirring frame dragging
physicsSplit.nonPromotion: fitting geopotential harmonics does not by itself test the gravitomagnetic coefficient

gravityProbeB.meaning: the measured gyroscope drift is compatible with GR and separates geodetic from frame-dragging precession

timeReversal.statement: a rotating source selects a state with J not equal to zero, but the underlying classical equations can remain T symmetric because T maps J to -J and reverses the associated precession

spin23.requiredDerivation: solve the candidate field equations for a stationary rotating source and recover the GR g_0i/spin-connection coefficient, including torsion or extra-field corrections
spin23.whyNotUnique: Cartan packaging of omega and e does not determine the action coefficients; ordinary GR and many equivalent formulations reproduce the same weak-field effect
spin23.falsifier: a derived frame-dragging coefficient or radial dependence outside experimental bounds after the same mass-multipole and non-gravitational systematics are fitted

decision: Lense-Thirring is the first clean vector-sector gravity benchmark for a Spin(2,3) Cartan completion, but agreement is a necessary GR recovery test rather than evidence selecting Spin(2,3)
